entry.title: Why LLMs cannot handle legal deadlines (and how to fix it with MCP)
entry.summary: Large Language Models are notoriously bad at arithmetic and temporal logic. While they excel at linguistic nuance, asking an agent to calculate a US federal court filing deadline is essentially inviting a hallucination into your workflow. Even with sophisticated prompting, the model struggles with the intersection of arbitrary integer offsets (like '21 days') and the non-linear reality of human calendars—weekends and federal holidays. A lawyer or a paralegal doesn't just need to add 21 to a date; they need to navigate a landscape of statutory rules, bank holidays, and weekend shifts. If an AI agent miscalculates a single deadline due to a missed Independence Day or a Sunday roll-over, the consequence isn't just a bug; it is professional negligence. entry.summary: Select a standby API credential at runtime from a versioned control record to change tenant access without a deploy. Make each switch attributable to an authorized actor.
